classification.difficultyReason: Choose the appropriate right-triangle ratio and invert or rearrange it; the hardest part first recognises the right triangle made by perpendicular rhombus diagonals. This is routine linked geometric and trigonometric reasoning for a prepared student.

content.prompt: Find the value of each pronumeral. Calculate values to one decimal place.

spec.description: Right triangle with right angle at the lower-left vertex, hypotenuse 9.5, opposite side 6.5 and unknown angle theta at the rightmost vertex.
spec.answerVisibility: Only the given lengths and unknown angle are visible.

spec.description: Right triangle with vertical left side 4.2, horizontal base x, right angle at bottom left and 35 degrees at top left.

Rhombus with double equal-side ticks on all four sides and both diagonals. Top side is x. The angle between the top side and the diagonal to the lower-right vertex is 20 degrees. A parallel dimension arrow measures only the upper-left vertex to the intersection of the diagonals, labelled 4.6.
spec.mathematics: The diagonals of a rhombus are perpendicular. The half-diagonal 4.6 is adjacent to 20 degrees and x is the hypotenuse.
spec.answerVisibility: The right angle at the diagonal intersection is inferred, not added as a supplied given.

answer.short:
$x\approx4.9$

Use the right triangle formed by the perpendicular diagonals of the rhombus.
answer.worked:
The four equal sides form a rhombus, whose diagonals intersect at right angles.

$$\begin{align*}\cos20^\circ&=\frac{4.6}{x}\\x&=\frac{4.6}{\cos20^\circ}\\x&\approx4.9\end{align*}$$
